description: pm-paper.py has ZERO automated tests (no test_pm_paper.py, no fixtures). book()'s best_bid/best_ask extraction assumes bids[-1] is the best bid and asks[-1] is the best ask ('bids, asks = b.get("bids") or [], b.get("asks") or []; best_bid = float(bids[-1]["price"]) ...; best_ask = float(asks[-1]["price"])'). This ordering assumption about the Polymarket CLOB /book response is asserted with a comment but never locked down by a fixture test. If the CLOB API's asks/bids arrays are ordered the opposite way for either side, best_ask would silently resolve to the WORST ask instead of the best, corrupting every paper entry_price, every recorded edge (model_p - entry), and every mark-to-market PnL computed downstream in mark()/resolve() — with no test to catch the regression either now or if Polymarket ever changes response ordering.

evidence.snippet:
def book(token_id):
    b = get(CLOB + token_id)
    bids, asks = b.get("bids") or [], b.get("asks") or []
    best_bid = float(bids[-1]["price"]) if bids else None
    best_ask = float(asks[-1]["price"]) if asks else None
